title: The Mandibular Retrusion Appliance (MRA) as a novel treatment for Class III patients
summary:
The mandibular retraction appliance (MRA) is a fixed orthodontic device designed for the treatment of patients with a mild to moderate form of underbite (Angle Class III). It works similarly to another device called MARA, but in the opposite way. The appliance is manufactured using modern laser technology and was developed in collaboration with the company orthoLIZE. There is also the possibility of combining the devices to move the lower jaw, thus correcting asymmetrical tooth alignments.

The goal of the study is to gather initial clinical experiences with the MRA and a combination of MARA and MRA. The study will investigate how well the devices are accepted by patients, how often defects occur, and what treatment outcomes can be expected. Additionally, it will examine the criteria that must be considered when selecting patients to ensure successful treatment with the appliance.

interventions.name: Patients with moderate Class III-malocclusion are treated with MRA

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
- permanent dentition 
- little to no residual growth
- maximum negative overjet of -2 mm
- a mesial bite less than 4 mm from Class I

For MARA/MRA patients: 
-asymmetric occlusion up to 4 mm form Class I per side
- midline shifts up to 3 mm
Exclusion criteria:
Foreseeable need for surgical intervention (orthognathic surgery, camouflage treatmenr)
